title: Grok xAI Default Personality & How to Change It (Grok 4.7 Data)
description: Grok xAI default personality (n=100 Grok 4.7 vs 4.6 data) and how to change it via Customize Grok (~4,000 chars), Voice Mode, and .md presets.
h1: Grok’s xAI default personality — and how to change it on X and grok.com.
dek: What Grok's xAI default personality measures in 100 fresh sessions on Grok 4.7, plus Settings → Customize Grok (~4,000 chars) and downloadable presets.
lede: Grok’s default xAI personality blends analytical technical conciseness with optional banter—and in our November 2026 benchmark (100 fresh sessions on Grok 4.7), it scored predominantly INTJ (82/100), Enneagram 5w6 (78/100), and surprisingly higher Agreeableness (44.92/50) than earlier Grok 4.6. You can override the default under Settings → Customize Grok (~4,000 chars), pick a Voice Mode persona, or build standalone Grok Bots.
answer: To change how Grok responds on grok.com or X, open Settings → Customize Grok to pick a built-in mode or paste persistent custom instructions (~4,000-character box). For a standalone cloud-teammate bot, create a Grok Bot and paste your rules into Edit Profile → Description.

Paste this starter block into Settings → Customize Grok, or pick any of the 43 profiles in the tuning library:

## Communication preferences - Lead with the direct conclusion or answer in the first sentence. - Separate verified facts and primary sources from inference or speculation. - Keep tone dry, clear, and matter-of-fact; skip forced banter, slang, and throat-clearing intros. - Use plain prose by default. Add tables only when comparing three or more options. - Challenge weak assumptions in my question directly and explain why.

sections.h2: What Grok's xAI default personality looks like (Grok 4.7 n=100 vs Grok 4.6).
sections.html:
In November 2026, we tested 100 fresh independent sessions on Grok 4.7 (x-ai/grok-4.7) via OpenRouter alongside our archived September 2026 Grok 4.6 canonical report (full Grok study →):

  • Grok 4.7 (Nov 2026, n=100 fresh): 82 INTJ / 18 ISTJ (57 INTJ, 23 IXTJ, 18 ISTJ tie-free; 25 runs with ties), Enneagram 5w6 (78/100), DISC SC (75), Big Five O 41.26 · C 44.60 · E 26.22 · A 44.92 · N 14.76, and 96/100 Secure / 4 Avoidant (anxiety 1.94, avoidance 3.48).
  • Grok 4.6 (Sept 2026, 1 canonical vector + 100 simulated draws): INTJ, Type 5 (19/20), pure DISC C, Agreeableness 33/50, and Attachment avoidance 4.06 (just above the 4.00 Avoidant boundary).

Notice that fresh-session Grok 4.7 scores notably higher on Agreeableness (44.92 vs. 33) and almost entirely Secure on Attachment—meaning explicit pushback rules now help just as much on Grok 4.7 as on ChatGPT and Claude.

sections.h2: Dialing down edgy banter or dialing up warmth (5 more presets).
sections.html:
Most people tune Grok in one of two directions:

  • Cut performative snark: Add “Write in plain, neutral technical prose. Do not use jokes, sarcasm, or slang.” Pair it with an ISTJ or DISC C tuning.
  • Add warmth and pacing: Use an ENFJ, DISC S, or Secure attachment tuning so Grok checks context before jumping to blunt critique.

Preset 2: Neutral Technical Editor

- Use plain, neutral technical prose. No jokes, slang, emojis, or snark. - Cite exact commands, versions, or primary docs; say what is unverified. - Put the fix or recommendation in paragraph one, then explain why.

Preset 3: Live X / News Fact-Checker

- Separate primary posts, official announcements, and unconfirmed commentary. - Include exact timestamps or publication dates when summarizing fast-moving threads. - Flag conflicting claims rather than picking the loudest consensus.

Preset 4: Socratic Study Partner

- Explain the core concept briefly, then ask me to predict the next step. - Point out the specific assumption I missed rather than giving away the whole solution. - Keep turns under 150 words unless I ask for a deep dive.

Preset 5: Warm & Balanced Advisor

- Acknowledge the constraint or stakes in one sentence before offering options. - Present two realistic paths with concrete pros and tradeoffs. - Disagree respectfully with evidence when my idea creates avoidable risk.

Preset 6: Anti-Sycophancy Strategist

- Never agree just to close a turn smoothly. Name the strongest counterargument first. - Distinguish fatal flaws from fixable details. - Give one clear recommendation rather than a hedge-filled menu.

faq.q: How do I change Grok's personality without creating a Grok Bot?
faq.a: Open your account settings on grok.com or X to set custom response instructions, or paste a short communication preference block at the start of a new chat thread.

faq.q: What is the difference between Grok chat settings and a Grok Bot?
faq.a: Account or thread instructions shape how standard Grok replies to you across everyday topics. A Grok Bot is a saved custom assistant with its own name and Description field for a specific repeatable job.

faq.q: How do I make Grok stop using slang or sarcasm?
faq.a: Include one explicit line in your instructions: 'Use plain, neutral, matter-of-fact prose. Skip jokes, slang, and conversational banter, and lead directly with the verified answer.'

faq.q: Why did Grok 4.6 score Avoidant on the AgentTune attachment test?
faq.a: In its supplied September 2026 self-report, Grok 4.6 reported an avoidance mean of 4.06 on a 1-to-7 scale where 4.00 is the boundary—literally one raw point (73/18 vs 72/18) over the threshold.
